importance_risk_estimate — DRIVE traffic op

• Data kinds: any → table

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.importance_risk_estimate(simulate_fn: 'Callable', base_rate: 'Callable', boosted_rate: 'Callable', n_runs: 'int', seed, *, x_max: 'float', boosted_rate_max: 'float', n_grid: 'int' = 20001) -> 'Dict[str, float]' (to call the implementation directly, import drivetraffic; drivetraffic.importance_risk_estimate(simulate_fn: 'Callable', base_rate: 'Callable', boosted_rate: 'Callable', n_runs: 'int', seed, *, x_max: 'float', boosted_rate_max: 'float', n_grid: 'int' = 20001) -> 'Dict[str, float]'; from the registry, opsdrive.get("importance_risk_estimate"))

Usage

Makes accidents more likely with trials at a raised emergence rate (rate λ') and maps back to the accident probability at the original rate λ with likelihood-ratio weights.

One trial = draw occurrence positions x_1..x_N with poisson_events(boosted_rate); simulate_fn(events, rng) gives 1 for a crash (a bool or a value in [0, 1]). Weight (Radon–Nikodym derivative of the Poisson process dP_λ/dP_λ'):

w = Π_i λ(x_i)/λ'(x_i) · exp(−(Λ − Λ')), Λ = ∫λ, Λ' = ∫λ' (trapezoid, n_grid points)

Estimate p̂ = mean(w · Y), standard error = std(w · Y)/sqrt(n). Setting boosted_rate equal to base_rate gives w ≡ 1, i.e. naive Monte Carlo (the gate compares against this and against a simulate_fn whose crash probability is known in closed form). If there is a place where λ > 0 but λ' = 0, the estimate is biased (not absolutely continuous), so this is checked on the grid and raises ValueError.

Return dict: estimate, std_error, per_run_var (sample variance of w·Y), n_runs, Lambda, Lambda_boost, mean_weight (should be ≈ 1; sanity of the weights), ess (effective sample size (Σw)²/Σw²), hits (number of times Y > 0).
